reason: The cited evidence (E1) describes sputter deposition of multicomponent boride films, not the FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys in question, and focuses on composition gradients and annealing rather than grain size control or magnetocaloric properties. It provides no support for any of the key premises linking nanocrystallinity to distributed nucleation, reduced hysteresis, or enhanced cooling efficiency.
premises: Nanocrystalline microstructure with high grain boundary density can be achieved in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type films
High grain boundary density facilitates distributed nucleation during the magnetostructural transition
Distributed nucleation broadens the transition and reduces hysteresis
Reduced hysteresis and broadened transition enhance low-field magnetic cooling efficiency
